protocol.description:
The barmaid protocol is an internal protocol for barmaids to report readiness for work and other statistics.
Barmaids are started by the tavern. This protocol is available only on the private control channel established for that child at startup, with the tavern as client and the barmaid as server. It must not be advertised or accepted on application-facing connections, including those of unsandboxed applications. The channel authenticates both participants; a process name, executable path, or claimed protocol name is not sufficient authentication.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_barmaid_manager_v1
object.description: This object is a core manager object bound upon creation.

s2c.name: ready
s2c.description:
This barmaid is ready to serve beer.
Sent once initialization completes and in response to request_status while ready. Readiness lasts for this control connection; a barmaid that can no longer serve must close it, so the tavern can withdraw its services.

c2s.name: request_status
c2s.description: Request the current status. A ready barmaid responds with the ready event. This request is valid before readiness; no response is sent while starting. The eventual ready event is still sent when initialization completes.

c2s.name: update_tavern_environment
c2s.description:
Forward the environment update already validated and authorized by the tavern's core protocol. Only the authenticated tavern may send this request; a caller's ordinary permission bypass does not authorize direct access.
The array, name, and value rules of the core request apply, including the maximum of 9999 elements per array. Validate the complete update before applying it; malformed updates are protocol errors. This request is valid before ready so the tavern can provide startup display configuration. It does not cause another permission prompt.

arg.name: env_names
arg.summary: An array of environment variable names

arg.name: env_values
arg.summary: An array of environment variable values
